requirement: Produce a revenue matrix with one row per product and one column per calendar month, zero where nothing sold, plus grand totals on both axes.
skeleton: A TOTAL_LABEL constant and revenue_matrix deriving a YYYY-MM month column and calling pivot_table with sum aggregation, fill_value 0 and margins named total.
caption: A product by month revenue matrix built with pandas pivot_table. revenue_matrix(sales) adds a month column formatted from the parsed date as YYYY-MM so columns sort chronologically, then pivots with index product, columns month, values amount and aggfunc sum so several lines in one month add up. fill_value 0 turns product and month combinations with no sales into zero instead of NaN, and margins True with margins_name set to the TOTAL_LABEL constant total appends a total row and a total column holding the sums. The fixture asserts that the rows are cup, ink, pen and total and the columns are 2024-01, 2024-02, 2024-03 and total, that two pen lines in January sum to 15, that cup reads 0, 20, 0, 20 with no NaN anywhere, and that the total column is 20, 7, 22, 49 and the total row is 18, 24, 7, 49.

constraints: Rows are products and columns are months
Month labels are YYYY-MM so they sort chronologically
Multiple lines in a cell are summed
A total row and column hold the margins

rationale.teaches: Choose the aggfunc, fill_value and margins explicitly and use sortable period labels so a pivot is directly usable as a report.
rationale.why: pivot_table averages by default, leaves NaN holes for empty cells, and month names sort alphabetically so February precedes January.

ops.docstring: Build a product-by-month revenue matrix with pivot_table.

ops.source:
def revenue_matrix(sales: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Rows are products, columns are YYYY-MM months, cells are summed revenue."""
    frame = sales.assign(month=pd.to_datetime(sales["date"]).dt.strftime("%Y-%m"))
    return frame.pivot_table(
        index="product",
        columns="month",
        values="amount",
        aggfunc="sum",
        fill_value=0,
        margins=True,
        margins_name=TOTAL_LABEL,
    )

candidates.why_wrong: Products without sales in a month show NaN instead of zero.
A month with several sales shows only the largest line, not the sum.
The matrix has no total row or total column.
Month-name columns sort alphabetically, putting Feb before Jan.
The matrix is transposed with months as rows and products as columns.
